target: Вы говорите по-английски или только по-русски?
english: Do you speak English or only Russian?
tip: After говорите (govorite = you speak), a language takes the по- adverb: по-английски (po-angliyski), по-русски (po-russki), not the noun form.

target: Брат ездит на работу на велосипеде.
english: My brother rides his bicycle to work.
tip: 'By' a vehicle uses на (na) plus the prepositional: на велосипеде (na velosipede = by bicycle). Same на (na) as 'on', different job.

target: Старший брат помогает младшему с уроками.
english: The older brother helps the younger one with homework.
tip: помогать (pomogat' = to help) takes a dative object with no 'to': помогает младшему (pomogaet mladshemu = helps the younger one), with the -ему (-emu) ending.

target: Я не хочу ни чай, ни кофе.
english: I want neither tea nor coffee.
tip: The pair ни...ни (ni...ni = neither...nor) still needs не (ne) on the verb: не хочу (ne khochu = I don't want). Russian keeps both negatives.

target: Коллега, с которой я работаю, очень умная.
english: The colleague with whom I work is very smart.
tip: After с (s = with), the noun goes instrumental: с которой (s kotoroy = with whom). которой is the instrumental of который (kotoryy = which).

target: Откуда вы и какой у вас родной язык?
english: Where are you from and what is your native language?
tip: Откуда (Otkuda = from where) asks origin, unlike где (gde = where) for location and куда (kuda = where to) for destination.

english: He works harder than anyone else.
tip: 'Than anyone' after a comparative is just the genitive: усерднее всех (userdneye vsekh = harder than everyone). No separate word for 'than'.
зовут (zovut = they call) is a subjectless they-form, so Как вас зовут (kak vas zovut) is literally how they call you.
The frame по (po) plus a -ски (-ski) ending means in a language: по-английски (po-angliyski = in English), always one lowercase word.
написал (napisal) is perfective, presenting the writing as one finished act: Кто написал (kto napisal = who wrote) this book.
After numbers five and up the counted noun goes genitive plural: пятнадцать процентов (pyatnadtsat protsentov = fifteen percent).
Seasons take the instrumental to mean in that season: весной (vesnoy = in spring), with no preposition.
Неужели (neuzheli) opens a question of disbelief, meaning really or you cannot be serious: Неужели он уже уехал (neuzheli on uzhe uekhal).
Possession puts the owner in genitive after the thing owned: дом моего брата (dom moego brata = my brother's house).
Feminine nouns in -а (a) shift to -у (u) as a direct object: читает книгу (chitaet knigu = reads a book).

english: When does the next bus leave?
tip: The -ся (-sya) on отправляется (otpravlyaetsya = departs) makes the verb act on itself, so it takes no object.

english: I saw the work through to the end.
tip: до (do = up to) takes the genitive: до конца (do kontsa = to the end).
давай (davay = let us) plus a we-form verb makes a suggestion: давай встретимся (davay vstretimsya = let's meet).
о (o = about) takes the prepositional case: о древней истории (o drevney istorii = about ancient history).
Negated existence forces the genitive: нет свободных мест (net svobodnykh mest = there are no free seats).

english: My friend has a country house.
tip: Russian has no verb to have, it uses у (u) plus genitive: у друга есть (u druga est = the friend has).

target: Доброе утро, кофе уже готов на столе.
english: Good morning, the coffee is already ready on the table.
tip: на (na = on) takes the prepositional case for location: на столе (na stole = on the table). The base form стол (stol) shifts to столе.

target: Я не буду есть эту кашу.
english: I will not eat this porridge.
tip: Imperfective future is буду/будешь (budu/budesh) plus an infinitive; the verb itself does not change: буду есть (budu yest = will eat).
Нет (net = there isn't) forces genitive: ничего невозможного (nichego nevozmozhnogo = nothing impossible), not a nominative form.
Откуда (otkuda = from where) asks where motion starts, куда (kuda = where to) asks the destination. Both go with motion verbs.
картой (kartoy = by card) is instrumental: paying by means of something uses the instrumental form with no preposition. Base карта (karta) becomes картой.
Что это за (chto eto za = what kind of) keeps the noun nominative: что это за здание (zdanie = building), not a genitive form.
по-русски (po-russki = in Russian) is an adverb, not a noun. Use it with говорю (govoryu = speak); there is no separate word for the language itself.
ничего (nichego = nothing) still needs не (ne = not) on the verb: ничего не понимаю (ne ponimayu = don't understand). Russian keeps both negatives.
домой (domoy = homeward) marks motion toward home. Being at home would be дома (doma = at home). Different words for going versus being.
